text.arabic_uthmani: أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُزْجِى سَحَابًۭا ثُمَّ يُؤَلِّفُ بَيْنَهُۥ ثُمَّ يَجْعَلُهُۥ رُكَامًۭا فَتَرَى ٱلْوَدْقَ يَخْرُجُ مِنْ خِلَٰلِهِۦ وَيُنَزِّلُ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مِن جِبَالٍۢ فِيهَا مِنۢ بَرَدٍۢ فَيُصِيبُ بِهِۦ مَن يَشَآءُ وَيَصْرِفُهُۥ عَن مَّن يَشَآءُ ۖ يَكَادُ سَنَا بَرْقِهِۦ يَذْهَبُ بِٱلْأَبْصَٰرِ

words.gloss_range: negative jussive particle inside a rhetorical seeing formula
words.prose: {{ar:لَمْ}} ({{tr:lam}}) opens the ayah inside a rhetorical question: formal negation and jussive government do not ask for new information, but press the addressee to acknowledge what is being shown. The particle makes the cloud scene an addressed sight-demonstration after the prior dominion statement (24:42).

topics.headline: rhetorical sight summons
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah begins as compelled recognition, not as a neutral question about weather.
topics.reason: The particle governs the following verb as jussive and, with interrogative force, launches a familiar recognition formula whose expected answer is affirmation.

words.gloss_range: seeing that includes observation, recognition, and reflective judgment in the opening formula
words.root_gloss_range: vision and considered perception; local grammar selects addressed seeing under jussive negation

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: later indicative seeing in the same ayah's vision arc

words.prose: {{ar:تَرَ}} ({{tr:tara}}) carries the addressee in the verb itself and appears in the clipped jussive form governed by the opening particle. Its seeing is broader than eyesight alone: the ayah asks the hearer to observe the cloud process and to recognize the agency behind it, while the later {{ar:تَرَى}} ({{tr:tarā}}) and final sight noun complete a vision arc from summoned sight to sight nearly taken.

topics.headline: addressed reflective seeing
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the opening seeing is personal and reflective, and that the ayah will end by threatening the very faculty it first summons.
topics.reason: QAC supports second-person jussive form, while the CRITICAL rows coherently connect the root's seeing/judgment range with the ayah-level vision frame.

words.gloss_range: assertive subordinator making the divine-action chain the content of seeing
words.prose: {{ar:أَنَّ}} ({{tr:ʾanna}}) makes the weather sequence the asserted content of the opening seeing. The particle does not simply introduce a loose next clause; it gathers the long chain of divine actions under what the addressee is being asked to recognize.

topics.headline: asserted seen content
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the cloud, rain, hail, and sight sequence is framed as one demonstrable fact under the seeing summons.
topics.reason: The particle governs the following accusative subject and gives the divine-action sequence a single subordinate, assertive frame.

words.gloss_range: proper divine name in accusative under the subordinator, supplying the named agent for the whole chain
words.root_gloss_range: divine name with worship/refuge and disputed bewilderment associations; local function is named divine agency
words.prose: {{ar:ٱللَّهَ}} ({{tr:Allāha}}) is accusative because it is governed by the subordinator, yet semantically it is the single named actor behind the subsequent verbs. Once the name is stated, later 3ms verbs can carry the same agent silently, so the weather never becomes an independent force; the formula also echoes the nearby bird-flight and glorification sign frame in 24:41.

topics.headline: single named agent
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that all the meteorological movement remains grammatically tied to one explicit divine actor.
topics.reason: The accusative proper name is the governed subject of the subordinate clause and the implicit subject of the later divine-action verbs.

topics.headline: nearby formula echo
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that this weather demonstration belongs beside the bird-flight and glorification sign frame of 24:41.
topics.reason: The concrete 24:41 echo is explicit in the source rows; derivational pressure around the divine name is kept as register, not as a replacement for the local proper-name function.

words.gloss_range: caused, measured propulsion of cloud movement
words.root_gloss_range: rare gentle driving or urging; local Form IV makes God cause the cloud to move
words.prose: {{ar:يُزْجِى}} ({{tr:yuzjī}}) begins the process with caused, measured propulsion rather than violent driving. The same named divine subject continues without being restated, and the rare motion root can align cloud-driving here with ship-driving across the sea in 17:66.

topics.headline: gentle caused propulsion
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the first cloud verb is a specialized word for guided, gradual movement under divine agency.
topics.reason: Form IV and the rare root profile both support caused propulsion, while the 3ms subject continues the named divine agent.

topics.headline: cross-medium driving
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that divine propulsion is pictured across mediums, with ships in 17:66 and clouds here moving under one guidance field.
topics.reason: The cited 17:66 recurrence is concrete and supports a controlled comparison without making it govern the local parse.

words.gloss_range: an indefinite collective cloud-mass, named with dragged-motion pressure
words.root_gloss_range: dragging, drawing along, withdrawal; local noun is the cloud as a movable collective body
words.prose: {{ar:سَحَابًا}} ({{tr:saḥāban}}) is indefinite and collective: the ayah shows a general cloud-mass, not one named cloud, and later singular pronouns can still treat its many parts as one body. Its root pressure reinforces the motion image, since the object being propelled is itself named through drawing or dragging along.

topics.headline: collective dragged cloud
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the cloud is both a general observable mass and a moving body whose name echoes the preceding propulsion verb.
topics.reason: The noun is accusative indefinite collective, and the later singular suffixes support a mass-conceived referent with internal plurality.

topics.headline: cadence weight
topics.no_reader_payoff_reason: The vowel-cadence observation is decorative after the collective motion topic already preserves the reader-facing cloud payoff.
topics.reason: The sound row adds no distinct lexical or structural payoff needed for this prose layer.

words.gloss_range: delayed sequence marker moving from propulsion to composition
words.prose: {{ar:ثُمَّ}} ({{tr:thumma}}) marks the first deliberate interval in the cloud sequence. The movement from propulsion to composition is staged, and the repeated particle will make the formation unfold as drive, compose, then heap rather than as one instant.

topics.headline: first delayed stage
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that cloud formation is presented as a measured sequence with visible phases.
topics.reason: The conjunction separates the first two divine verbs and, with the second occurrence, creates the three-stage architecture.

words.gloss_range: intensive composing or bringing into coherent relation
words.root_gloss_range: joining, familiarity, affinity, composition; local Form II makes active composition of cloud parts
words.prose: {{ar:يُؤَلِّفُ}} ({{tr:yuʾallifu}}) turns moving cloud material into a composed relation. Form II makes the joining active and intensive, and the root's affinity field means the cloud parts are not merely thrown together; they are brought into ordered coherence. The same root can describe the composing of hearts in 3:103 and 8:63, but here the local scene remains meteorological.

topics.headline: intensive cloud composition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the cloud mass is organized into relation, not merely gathered as loose vapor.
topics.reason: Form II supports intensive causative composition, and the following interval phrase confirms that relations among cloud parts are in view.

topics.headline: heart composition echo
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that a root used for composing hearts in 3:103 and 8:63 gives the cloud scene a relational, harmonizing pressure.
topics.reason: The echo is valid as a root-level comparison, but local grammar selects physical cloud composition rather than social reconciliation as the active sense.

words.gloss_range: internal between-space bound by suffix to the collective cloud
words.root_gloss_range: between, separation, distinction, clarification; local use keeps intervals inside one composed cloud body
words.prose: {{ar:بَيْنَهُ}} ({{tr:baynahū}}) binds the interval to the cloud by suffix. Composition does not erase separation: the cloud remains one referent while its parts still have internal between-spaces that can be managed and made clear enough for later emergence.

topics.headline: internal managed interval
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the cloud is composed without losing its internal separations; the formed mass still contains ordered intervals.
topics.reason: The suffix returns to the collective cloud, and the root's interval/distinction field fits the syntax between composing and piling.

words.gloss_range: second delayed sequence marker before the heaping stage
words.prose: {{ar:ثُمَّ}} ({{tr:thumma}}) repeats the delayed transition and opens a third stage. The cloud is not just moved and composed; only after another interval is it rendered into a piled mass.

topics.headline: second delayed stage
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a deliberate three-step architecture: propulsion, composition, then accumulation.
topics.reason: The second occurrence separates the composition verb from the rendering verb and repeats the measured pacing created at word 7.

topics.headline: sound refrain
topics.reason: The sound observation duplicates the staged-refrain payoff already preserved by the sequence topic.

words.gloss_range: transformative making, with the cloud suffix as object and the next noun as resulting state
words.root_gloss_range: making, rendering, appointing, creating; local construction selects rendering an existing cloud into a state
words.prose: {{ar:يَجْعَلُهُ}} ({{tr:yajʿaluhū}}) keeps the same cloud as object through the attached suffix and gives it a resulting state in the next word. The verb is not creating from nothing here; it renders the already-propelled and composed cloud into a heaped form under the same unstated divine subject.

topics.headline: transformative rendering
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the cloud's identity continues while its state changes into a piled mass.
topics.reason: The root is broad, so the topic is narrowed to rendering because the construction has an existing pronoun object and an accusative result complement.

words.gloss_range: piled, layered accumulated mass as the cloud's resulting state
words.root_gloss_range: heaping and accumulation; local noun names a vertical, dense mass rather than generic gathering
words.prose: {{ar:رُكَامًا}} ({{tr:rukāman}}) names the result as piled accumulation, not a loose collection. The rare root makes the cloud dense, layered, and quasi-solid, preparing the later image of mountain-like sky formations and the release of rain from within them; it can also associate this cloud mass with sky-fragment heaping imagery in 52:44.

topics.headline: vertical accumulated mass
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the cloud is transformed into a dense layered body capable of source, channel, and payload imagery.
topics.reason: The accusative indefinite complement names the resulting state, and the root evidence supports vertical accumulation rather than generic collection.

topics.headline: sky mass echo
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the rare heaping root can associate cloud mass here with sky-fragment imagery in 52:44.
topics.reason: The source gives 52:44 as a concrete comparison; it is useful as an echo while the local sense remains heaped cloud.

topics.headline: sound heaviness
topics.reason: The phonetic rows reinforce weight but add no independent payoff after the lexical accumulation topic.

words.gloss_range: immediate consequence marker pivoting from cloud formation to human observation
words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) changes the pacing from delayed formation to immediate result. Once the cloud has become piled, the next thing is not another hidden stage but the addressee seeing the rain emerge.

topics.headline: immediate visible result
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the pivot from God's hidden formation process into the observer's visible evidence.
topics.reason: The conjunction follows the delayed sequence and marks the seeing clause as consequence of the completed heaping stage.

words.gloss_range: direct indicative seeing of the rain output
words.root_gloss_range: seeing and perception; local form is indicative empirical witnessing after the formation result
words.prose: {{ar:تَرَى}} ({{tr:tarā}}) repeats the addressed seeing root but now as indicative observation: the hearer is positioned at the moment where rain becomes visible. The ayah's vision frame therefore moves from opening reflective seeing, to this empirical seeing, to the final threat against sight itself.

topics.headline: empirical seeing pivot
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the same addressee who was challenged to recognize is now made witness to a concrete rain-output point.
topics.reason: The indicative form contrasts with the earlier jussive and governs the visible rain object in the next word.

words.gloss_range: definite, specialized cloud-rain output
words.root_gloss_range: rain and approaching or drawing near; local noun is the recognizable rain emerging from cloud gaps
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْوَدْقَ}} ({{tr:al-wadqa}}) names the rain as a known output of the cloud process, not as generic precipitation detached from its source. The rare term keeps the rain tied to emergence from cloud gaps, and its approach-sense lets the visible output feel like moisture coming near from the formed mass.

topics.headline: specialized cloud rain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the rain is a precise, recognizable product of the cloud mechanism rather than a generic weather label.
topics.reason: Definiteness, rarity evidence, and local collocation with emergence and interstice roots all support a specialized cloud-output sense.

words.gloss_range: intransitive emergence from an interior source
words.root_gloss_range: coming out, exiting, emergence; local Form I makes rain issue from cloud openings rather than merely fall
words.prose: {{ar:يَخْرُجُ}} ({{tr:yakhruju}}) makes the rain emerge from within rather than simply descend from above. The seen object becomes the semantic subject of an intransitive verb, so the cloud mass has an interior and channels through which the rain comes out, reversing the withheld-sight pressure of the dark-cloud scene in 24:40.

topics.headline: interior emergence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices rain as a product issuing from inside the cloud's structure, not merely falling in a flat vertical description.
topics.reason: Form I intransitive emergence and the following source phrase support interior-to-exterior movement.

topics.headline: darkness reversal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a same-surah contrast with 24:40: where that cloud-darkness scene withholds sight, this emergence scene produces visible rain.
topics.reason: The source row gives the concrete 24:40 comparison, and it functions as contrast without overriding the local emergence parse.

words.gloss_range: source preposition beginning the nested source chain
words.prose: {{ar:مِنْ}} ({{tr:min}}) marks the rain's source in the cloud's openings. It also starts the ayah's repeated source-chain, which moves from gaps, to sky, to mountains, to hail substance.

topics.headline: first source min
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the preposition turns rain emergence into sourced motion from inside the cloud, then begins a larger telescoping source pattern.
topics.reason: The preposition governs the interstice phrase and is the first of the four source/specification prepositions in the ayah.

words.gloss_range: its interstices or openings, with variant pressure between many gaps and one narrowed channel
words.root_gloss_range: gaps, penetration, openings, and intimacy by penetration; local use names cloud channels
words.prose: {{ar:خِلَالِهِ}} ({{tr:khilālihī}}) makes the piled cloud permeable: rain comes through its internal openings. Variant forms can narrow many interstices to a single channel, but the local payoff remains that the dense mass has structured passageways, not a blank surface.

topics.headline: permeable cloud channels
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the cloud as dense yet channelled, with rain piercing through structured openings.
topics.reason: The governed phrase after source preposition and the root's gap/penetration field support channel-structure.

topics.headline: gap variant pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that accepted form variation tests whether rain is pictured through multiple openings or a concentrated channel.
topics.reason: Variant pressure is useful for contrast, but the canonical local form remains the base for the prose.

topics.headline: intimacy and sound
topics.reason: The intimacy and phonetic observations are secondary extensions of the penetration/opening image already retained.

words.gloss_range: coordination that links rain emergence to hail descent and shifts spatial axis
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) keeps the rain-emergence clause connected to the hail-descent clause. It can simply coordinate, and it can also leave overlap available, but its main payoff is the spatial reorientation from rain exiting through cloud gaps to hail descending from the sky.

topics.headline: linked precipitation axes
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that two precipitation scenes are linked while the ayah turns from internal emergence to vertical descent.
topics.reason: The conjunction coordinates the next divine verb with the preceding rain-emergence clause and allows, but does not require, simultaneity.

words.gloss_range: Form II sending down, staged or repeated descent
words.root_gloss_range: descent and sending down, especially divine delivery; local object is hail descent from sky formations
words.prose: {{ar:يُنَزِّلُ}} ({{tr:yunazzilu}}) resumes the same divine subject after the conjunction and makes hail descent an active sending-down from the sky owned in 24:42. The Form II surface favors staged or repeated descent, while the alternate Form IV reading exposes a simpler causative descent; the root also lets weather-descent stand near the Qur'anic revelation-descent vocabulary in passages such as 2:4, 3:3, and 97:1.

topics.headline: staged divine descent
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that hailfall is governed as a repeated or staged divine delivery, not an impersonal fall.
topics.reason: The Form II imperfect and pro-dropped subject support staged descent under the same divine actor.

topics.headline: descent root register
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that a root prominent in revelation-descent also describes weather sent from the owned sky of 24:42.
topics.reason: The revelation register is real root background, but local syntax selects hail descent from the sky rather than revealed text.

words.gloss_range: broad source preposition before the sky
words.prose: {{ar:مِنَ}} ({{tr:mina}}) opens the hail clause with a broad source: from the sky. The later source phrases then narrow that upper domain into mountains and hail.

topics.headline: broad sky source
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the source-chain zoom out from cloud gaps to the sky before narrowing again.
topics.reason: The preposition governs the sky noun as source and functions as the second layer in the four-part source structure.

words.gloss_range: definite visible sky as elevated source domain
words.root_gloss_range: elevation, sky, upper covering, and in some usage rain; local noun is the known sky-source
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلسَّمَاءِ}} ({{tr:al-samāʾi}}) makes the source a known, shared sky rather than an unnamed realm. The same elevated domain that stood in the prior dominion frame (24:42) becomes an experienced source of descent; rain-sense pressure may color the word, but the local phrase still points to the visible sky.

topics.headline: visible owned sky source
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that abstract dominion over the heavens becomes concrete action from the visible sky.
topics.reason: The noun is singular definite and governed by source preposition, narrowing the prior heavens frame of 24:42 into a visible sky-source.

topics.headline: rain sense pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the sky word can carry precipitation pressure while still functioning locally as the elevated source.
topics.reason: Lexical evidence allows rain associations, but the governed phrase and following nested source syntax keep visible sky as the local reference.

words.gloss_range: third source/specification preposition narrowing the sky-source into mountains
words.prose: {{ar:مِنْ}} ({{tr:min}}) narrows the broad sky-source into mountains. Its function can be read as source-origin or explanatory specification, but either way it pushes the reader deeper into the nested storm architecture.

topics.headline: source specification zoom
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the phrase both narrows the source and keeps a live source-versus-specification parse.
topics.reason: The preposition can plausibly mark origin or bayān; both readings keep the mountain phrase dependent within the source-chain.

words.gloss_range: indefinite plural mountains, locally mountain-like cloud formations within the sky
words.root_gloss_range: mountains, molding, formed disposition; local image gives clouds height, mass, and formed solidity
words.prose: {{ar:جِبَالٍ}} ({{tr:jibālin}}) makes the sky-source mountainous: indefinite plural formations, not one fixed earthly mountain. The metaphor gives cloud towers mass, height, and shaped solidity, and the molding sense of the root supports the image of storm architecture formed to contain hail.

topics.headline: sky mountain formations
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the storm is pictured as towering, massive cloud architecture rather than a flat sky.
topics.reason: The phrase is indefinite plural in the sky context, so the mountain image is narrowed to mountain-like cloud formations, not literal terrestrial mountains relocated into the sky.

topics.headline: molded solidity pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the mountain image carries formed solidity and reservoir capacity for the hail payload.
topics.reason: The root's mountain and molding branches cohere with the local container phrase and do not displace the cloud-formation reading.

topics.headline: sound weight
topics.reason: The phonetic weight row duplicates the already retained mass and solidity payoff.

words.gloss_range: locative containment, with feminine suffix referring to mountains or sky
words.prose: {{ar:فِيهَا}} ({{tr:fīhā}}) turns the sky-mountain image into a container. The suffix can route to the mountain formations or to the sky, but either way the hail is located inside the source domain rather than merely near it.

topics.headline: storm container
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the storm architecture has interior containment: the hail is housed within the sky-mountain scene.
topics.reason: The pronoun's exact antecedent is live, so the topic is narrowed to containment that survives both mountain and sky referent routes.

words.gloss_range: final partitive or material-specifying preposition landing the source-chain on hail
words.prose: {{ar:مِنْ}} ({{tr:min}}) completes the nested source chain by landing on hail. It can specify the material of the formations or mark a partitive payload within them, but in both readings the zoom ends on the storm's cold substance.

topics.headline: final hail specification
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the four-step source zoom closing on hail as the storm's specific payload or substance.
topics.reason: The final preposition can be partitive or explanatory, so it is narrowed to the shared payoff: content/material specification at the end of the min-chain.

words.gloss_range: hail or cold solid precipitation as the governed endpoint of the source chain
words.root_gloss_range: coldness, hail, cooling; local noun gives the descent hard material force

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: later lightning term paired with hail as a storm output

words.prose: {{ar:بَرَدٍ}} ({{tr:baradin}}) is the cold, solid payload at the end of the source chain. The word gives the descent material force before the striking verb arrives, and its near-sound relation with {{ar:بَرْقِهِ}} ({{tr:barqihī}}) later pairs cold impact with bright flash as two storm outputs.

topics.headline: cold solid payload
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the storm's payload is not neutral water but hard cold matter that can become an instrument of impact.
topics.reason: The genitive noun after the final source preposition names hail/coldness as the material endpoint.

topics.headline: hail lightning twinning
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that hail and lightning are paired by near-sound while their effects diverge into impact and brilliance.
topics.reason: The b-r frame comparison is local because the lightning noun appears later in the same ayah and the effects are distinct storm outputs.

words.gloss_range: immediate result marker from hail descent to impact
words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) makes striking the consequence of hail descent. It mirrors the earlier result marker before seeing: one pivot yields visible rain, the other yields physical impact.

topics.headline: impact result pivot
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah pairs two results: seeing rain and hail striking.
topics.reason: The conjunction marks consequence and structurally mirrors the earlier result conjunction before the human seeing clause.

words.gloss_range: causative targeted impact or befalling under divine agency
words.root_gloss_range: hitting the mark, befalling, pouring, correctness, affliction; local Form IV selects causing impact upon a target
words.prose: {{ar:يُصِيبُ}} ({{tr:yuṣību}}) makes the hail strike targeted rather than random. The Form IV verb keeps God as the implicit subject who causes the impact, while the root's hit-the-mark and affliction field lets the weather event become a selective befalling before the mirrored diversion clause reverses it.

topics.headline: targeted hail impact
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the hail's impact is directed through divine agency, not left to random collision.
topics.reason: Form IV and the following object frame support caused impact, while the repeated will formula controls target selection.

topics.headline: affliction field
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the hail strike belongs to a broader befalling-affliction vocabulary, linking physical weather to selective testing.
topics.reason: The affliction family survives as root pressure because local impact is explicitly selective and consequential.

words.gloss_range: instrumental preposition with suffix referring to hail or the wider precipitation event
words.prose: {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi}}) makes the hail, or the wider storm event, the instrument of striking. The suffix avoids repeating the payload noun while keeping physical means inside divine agency.

topics.headline: instrumental storm means
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that divine action works through a concrete storm instrument whose exact scope remains live.
topics.reason: The preposition is instrumental, but the suffix can refer narrowly to hail or more broadly to the precipitation process, so the topic is narrowed to shared instrumentality.

words.gloss_range: open relative target in the strike clause
words.prose: {{ar:مَنْ}} ({{tr:man}}) leaves the struck target unnamed. The person is defined only by the following will formula, and the same open relative frame will return for the spared target.

topics.headline: open struck target
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that target identity is withheld and selection is left inside the will formula.
topics.reason: The relative pronoun opens an unspecified target slot governed by the following verb.

words.gloss_range: divine willing in the first selection formula
words.root_gloss_range: willing and thingness; local verb marks volition governing the strike target
words.prose: {{ar:يَشَاءُ}} ({{tr:yashāʾu}}) closes the strike half of the selection frame. The subject remains the same implicit divine actor, and the root's will/thingness field places the weather event under volition rather than anonymous mechanics, within the surah's repeated vocabulary of selection and allocation.

topics.headline: first will selection
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the struck target is selected by divine will and that the same formula will govern the opposite outcome.
topics.reason: The 3ms verb completes the relative clause and shares the same implicit divine subject as the surrounding action chain.

topics.headline: surah volition network
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that this will formula belongs to a repeated surah-local vocabulary of selection and allocation.
topics.reason: The recurrence evidence is local to the surah and reinforces the formula without changing the selected sense.

words.gloss_range: coordination of opposite divine outcomes
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) coordinates striking and diverting as paired outcomes of one governed storm event. The conjunction does not merely add another clause; it builds the binary distribution of affliction and protection.

topics.headline: coordinated opposites
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that striking and sparing are coordinated under one agent rather than treated as unrelated weather outcomes.
topics.reason: The conjunction links the antithetical verbs and preserves one divine-governed distribution system.

words.gloss_range: turning or diverting the storm object away
words.root_gloss_range: turning, averting, managing, inflecting; local verb redirects the hail or storm process away from a target
words.prose: {{ar:يَصْرِفُهُ}} ({{tr:yaṣrifuhū}}) reverses the impact verb by turning the same storm object away. The suffix keeps the averted thing compactly present, while the root's management and turning field makes protection an active redirection of trajectory and connects hail-diversion with atmospheric turning such as wind-turning in 2:164 and 45:5.

topics.headline: active diversion
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that sparing is not absence of action but active turning-away of the same storm threat.
topics.reason: The exact suffix referent is live, so the topic is narrowed to what survives all routes: the storm object or effect is actively diverted.

topics.headline: atmospheric control field
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that hail-diverting sits within a wider root field of turning and managing atmospheric forces, as in wind-turning at 2:164 and 45:5.
topics.reason: The cited atmospheric parallels support root-level control vocabulary while local syntax selects diversion of the storm object.

words.gloss_range: away-from preposition marking avoidance of the spared target
words.prose: {{ar:عَنْ}} ({{tr:ʿan}}) is the small directional hinge from affliction to sparing. After the instrument preposition in the strike clause, this away-from preposition marks the target as avoided rather than hit.

topics.headline: away from hinge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the pivot from strike to protection is encoded at the level of preposition choice.
topics.reason: The preposition governs the second relative target and marks separation or avoidance in contrast with the earlier instrumental/toward relation.

words.gloss_range: second open relative target in the sparing clause
words.prose: {{ar:مَنْ}} ({{tr:man}}) repeats the open target frame, now after the away-from preposition. The spared person is no more identified than the struck person; the grammar stays symmetrical while the outcome reverses.

topics.headline: open spared target
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that both affliction and protection use the same unspecified target frame under will.
topics.reason: The repeated relative pronoun preserves syntactic symmetry between the strike and diversion clauses.

words.gloss_range: second divine willing formula governing the opposite outcome
words.root_gloss_range: willing and thingness; local verb marks one will behind both striking and diverting
words.prose: {{ar:يَشَاءُ}} ({{tr:yashāʾu}}) repeats the same form, subject, and formula for the opposite outcome. The verbs change from striking to diverting, but the willer does not, so one divine volition governs the bilateral distribution within the surah's repeated choice vocabulary.

topics.headline: one will opposite outcomes
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that affliction and sparing are not two kinds of agency but two outcomes under the same repeated will formula.
topics.reason: The second occurrence repeats the same verb form and implicit divine subject, with antithesis located in the surrounding verbs.

topics.headline: surah choice network
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the repeated volition formula participates in the surah's larger selection vocabulary.
topics.reason: The recurrence evidence is useful as a local thematic network while the immediate syntax remains the controlling evidence.

words.gloss_range: proximity verb: near-action that stops short of completion
words.root_gloss_range: nearly doing or approaching an action; local use puts the lightning flash at the threshold of removing sight
words.prose: {{ar:يَكَادُ}} ({{tr:yakādu}}) opens the closing luminosity clause with almost-action. The flash comes to the brink of taking sight but does not complete it, so the ayah lands on restrained threshold pressure after the long divine-action chain; the light-threshold echo with 24:35 intensifies that close.

topics.headline: near blinding threshold
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final action is suspended at the edge of sight-loss rather than completed.
topics.reason: The proximity verb governs the following removal verb and opens a closing clause that shifts from hail distribution to sight pressure.

topics.headline: light threshold echo
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the lightning near-blinding here shares a same-surah light-threshold pattern with the oil almost glowing in 24:35.
topics.reason: The source row supplies 24:35 as a concrete echo, and the comparison is limited to the shared near-action luminosity pattern.

words.gloss_range: flash or brilliance, nominative construct head of the lightning phrase
words.root_gloss_range: flash and brilliance, with variant pressure toward eminence or glory; local noun is the lightning flash as subject of near-removal
words.prose: {{ar:سَنَا}} ({{tr:sanā}}) is the nominative head of the construct phrase: the flash belongs specifically to the storm's lightning. As a rare, even hapax-like brilliance word, it concentrates the final light pressure, and the hamzated variant raises the register toward eminence without replacing the local flash sense.

topics.headline: construct flash subject
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the grammatical subject of near-removal is not lightning in general but the flash of its lightning.
topics.reason: QAC marks a nominative abstract noun followed by a genitive construct partner, matching the subject role in the near-removal clause.

topics.headline: hapax brilliance
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah reserves an unusually concentrated word for this final lightning brilliance.
topics.reason: The occurrence evidence supports marked rarity, which strengthens the final light-pressure payoff.

topics.headline: hamza variant register
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the hamzated reading lets physical brilliance approach a glory or eminence register while the canonical local sense remains flash.
topics.reason: The variant is useful as contrast, but it cannot override the standard local flash reading.

topics.headline: sound openness
topics.reason: The sound rows mainly decorate the retained contrast between smooth flash and hamzated register.

words.gloss_range: his or its lightning, singular construct with suffix tied to the storm system
words.root_gloss_range: lightning, flashing, gleaming, dazzled sight, sudden brightness; local noun supplies the cause of near sight-loss
words.prose: {{ar:بَرْقِهِ}} ({{tr:barqihī}}) makes the flash belong to the storm system through a suffix whose precise referent can be the cloud or hail process. The root already contains lightning and dazzled-sight pressure, so the cause of near-blinding is lexically prepared; variant plural readings multiply the discharges, while the local singular can concentrate the flash as one overwhelming brilliance. Its b-r frame also answers the earlier hail word, pairing cold solid impact with bright electrical flash as twin storm outputs.

topics.headline: storm owned lightning
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the lightning is not free-floating but belongs to the preceding storm process.
topics.reason: The suffix referent is live, so the topic is narrowed to storm-system possession rather than a single forced antecedent.

topics.headline: dazzled sight root
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the lightning root itself links the luminous cause with dazzled vision before the sight-removal idiom arrives.
topics.reason: Lexical evidence supports flashing and dazzled-sight associations, both coherent with the local near-blinding clause.

topics.headline: plural lightning variants
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that variant readings expose repeated discharges while the standard singular concentrates the event.
topics.reason: The variants are contrastive evidence, while the canonical local form remains singular in construct.

topics.headline: hail lightning pair
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that cold solid hail and bright lightning are paired as twin storm outputs through sound and field.
topics.reason: The local hail noun and lightning noun share the b-r frame and occur in the same storm sequence.

words.gloss_range: goes with or takes away in the idiom completed by the following preposition
words.root_gloss_range: going away, removal through motion, and gleaming gold homograph pressure; local idiom means nearly carrying sight off
words.prose: {{ar:يَذْهَبُ}} ({{tr:yadhhabu}}) turns motion into removal once the following preposition completes the idiom. In the lightning clause, the root's departure sense can brush against gleaming pressure from the gold homograph. The standard form pictures the flash going away with sight, while the causative variant makes it directly remove sight; either way the closing action drives toward the final word, sight itself.

topics.headline: motion to removal idiom
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that a simple motion verb becomes sight-removal through its idiomatic prepositional construction.
topics.reason: The following preposition and final object create the removal idiom, and the verb carries the closure toward the sight noun.

topics.headline: causative variant agency
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the variant shifts the action from idiomatic accompaniment to direct causation of sight-loss.
topics.reason: Variant evidence is valid for contrast, but the standard local form remains the Form I idiom with the following preposition.

topics.headline: gleaming removal pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a faint lexical pressure linking brilliance and departure in the lightning clause.
topics.reason: The gold homograph can color the lightning context, but it is secondary to the idiomatic removal construction.

words.gloss_range: preposition completing the removal idiom and marking the object carried off
words.prose: {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi}}) is not disposable here; it completes the removal idiom after the motion verb. Before the final sight noun, the preposition marks what is almost carried off and brings the ayah's seeing-frame to its terminal object.

topics.headline: removal idiom preposition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the preposition changes the verb from motion into taking-away and places sight at the ayah's final landing.
topics.reason: The preposition is required by the idiom and governs the final sight object.

words.gloss_range: definite plural sights or visual faculties as the threatened object
words.root_gloss_range: eyesight, perception, discernment, insight; local noun names collective sight nearly taken by lightning
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْأَبْصَارِ}} ({{tr:al-ʾabṣāri}}) closes the ayah on definite plural sight, not one observer's eye. The word gathers visual faculties collectively, can lean toward perception and insight, and completes the arc from the opening seeing summons through the middle seeing of rain to sight almost overwhelmed.

topics.headline: collective threatened sight
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that lightning threatens the collective faculty of sight and perception, not merely a single eye.
topics.reason: Definite plural morphology and root range support collective visual faculties as the object of the removal idiom.

topics.headline: vision arc closure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah's full seeing arc: sight invited, sight directed to rain, then sight nearly taken.
topics.reason: The row family explicitly links the opening, middle, and closing vision terms, and the final word supplies the threatened endpoint.

topics.headline: final sound closure
topics.reason: The sound observation is secondary to the stronger structural closure on sight.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The sequence yuzji -> yu'allifu baynahu -> yaj'aluhu rukaman -> al-wadq yakhruju min khilalihi.
baseline_models.mechanism: Gentle transport gathers dispersed cloud, composition joins its parts, transformation piles them, yet the resulting mass retains traversable gaps from which rain exits. Densification therefore creates a productive porous body rather than a sealed block.

activation_trace.role: Gentle pushing and driving supplies the controlled transport that starts the assembly.
The cloud as a body drawn through the air supplies the mobile material being worked.
Joining after dispersion and arranging unlike parts supplies the compositional operation.
Causing a thing to take on a state marks the phase change from gathered cloud to pile.
Heaping one part above another supplies density and vertical accumulation.
Descending rain supplies the useful output of the assembled mass.
Passage from an interior to an exterior makes the output an emergence, not a surface coating.
A gap and traversable interval supplies channels that remain inside the pile.

changed_reading.before: A succession of ordinary cloud, rain, and hail phenomena.
changed_reading.after: A staged material mechanism in which dispersed matter is transported, composed, densified, and made productive through retained internal channels.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: Yunazzilu ... min baradin, fa-yusibu bihi man yasha'u wa-yasrifuhu 'an man yasha'.
baseline_models.mechanism: The nested source chain culminates in a payload whose two outcomes are paired: it reaches a selected target or is turned away from one. Impact and non-impact are coordinated routing operations upon the same descending material.

activation_trace.role: Sending something down, including water, benefit, or affliction, supplies controlled delivery from above.
A high solid mass supplies the reservoir-like mountain form within the sky.
Cold and hail from cloud supplies the discrete descending payload.
Aiming and arriving at a target makes yusibu an exact landing rather than diffuse occurrence.
Will directed toward bringing about a thing governs both the hit and the deflection clauses.
Turning something back from a direction supplies the complementary non-impact route.

changed_reading.before: Hail happens to fall in some places and misses others.
changed_reading.after: One descending payload is selectively allocated: arrival and diversion are paired, intentional outcomes of a single routing system.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: Alam tara and fa-tara frame the process, but yakadu sana barqihi yadhhabu bil-absar turns eyesight from observer into endangered object.
baseline_models.mechanism: The ayah begins by recruiting sight and reflective seeing, repeats seeing at the moment rain emerges, then ends at a near-event where lightning radiance would remove sight. Evidence is visually offered while the visual faculty is shown to have an upper limit.

activation_trace.role: Eye-sight and insight jointly supply the faculty that observes both the whole process and its rain output.
The alerting force of ara'ayta makes the opening a demand for considered recognition, not passive looking.
Near-completion places loss of sight at a threshold rather than stating completed blindness.
Lightning's radiance supplies the intense luminous input at that threshold.
The branch of a startled, transfixed eye lets lightning and perceptual seizure converge at one root image.
Going away supplies the threatened removal of the observer's visual capacity.
The eye faculty is the instrument initially used and the final object placed at risk.
Heart-sight keeps the ending open to loss of discernment as well as sensory overload.

changed_reading.before: The weather is displayed so that an observer can see divine power.
changed_reading.after: The display tests the observer: perception must cross from sight to insight before dazzling evidence disables the very faculty receiving it.

context_deltas.mechanism: At 24:35 oil almost emits light without fire; at 24:40 layered covering makes a hand almost unseeable; at 24:43 lightning almost removes sight; and 24:44 turns alternation into an 'ibrah for possessors of sight. These matched near-constructions place the focus at the glare edge of a calibrated visibility spectrum.

activation_trace.role: Near-action supplies a lower luminous threshold where oil approaches giving light.
Spread radiance supplies beneficial illumination that nearly emerges even before fire.
An overlying cover supplies the opposite optical failure by blocking what lies beneath.
The negated near-action marks the hand as approaching, but not attaining, visibility.
Actual eye-seeing is the capacity suppressed by layered darkness.
Lightning radiance supplies the excessive-light endpoint of the scale.
The transfixed-eye branch makes glare a perceptual seizure rather than merely a bright object.
Eyesight is the measurable capacity threatened at the high end.
Taking one condition as a lesson for another supplies the crossing from optics to inference.
Heart-sight supplies the cognitive completion expected of possessors of vision.

structural_cues: The ordered sequence 24:35 -> 24:40 -> 24:43 -> 24:44 moves from near-light, through near-nonseeing, to near-blinding, then to lesson.
The repeated kada construction supplies matched thresholds rather than unrelated mentions of vision.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the three near-constructions and the final 'ibrah; I infer that they form one optical scale whose usable middle is guided perception. A live alternative is that each image independently marks power without a shared calibration mechanism.

changed_reading.before: The focus invites observation and ends with dangerous glare.
changed_reading.after: The focus occupies the upper threshold of a visibility system: too little light prevents sight, measured light guides, and excessive light defeats sight, so true seeing requires calibrated inference.

context_deltas.mechanism: The mirage at 24:39 offers a thirsty observer water-like shine with no water on arrival; the focus supplies rain that visibly exits a causal structure while also separating it from spectacular lightning; 24:45 then makes water the material of created creatures. The focus becomes the effective-water middle between deceptive appearance and generative consequence.

activation_trace.role: A shimmer that looks like water supplies appearance without material delivery.
Thirst supplies the need that makes bright appearance vulnerable to misrecognition.
Water as the expected substance is named but proves absent at the mirage.
Actual descending rain supplies the material counterpart to mirage-water.
Emergence from an interior supplies a visible causal path for the real water.
Lightning's flash supplies the spectacular surface that must not be confused with material efficacy.
Water now supplies the stated substrate from which living creatures are made.
Creative bringing-into-being supplies the downstream consequence that verifies water's efficacy.

structural_cues: 24:39 places absent apparent water before the focus, while 24:45 places creaturely formation from water after it.
Within 24:43, rain exits before lightning threatens sight, distinguishing material output from visual spectacle.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies mirage-water, causally emerging rain, lightning glare, and creation from water; I infer causal efficacy as the criterion separating appearance from substance. A live alternative is simple juxtaposition of signs without an epistemic test.

changed_reading.before: The focus is a detailed account of precipitation and hail.
changed_reading.after: The focus verifies effective water: unlike mirage it emerges through a traceable process, and unlike flash it has material continuity with the life made from water.

context_deltas.mechanism: The surah lowers only a portion of sight, guards vulnerable openings, distinguishes what appears from what stays hidden, and sets timed permission around private exposure. Against that context, the focus cloud is not simply open or closed: it is a boundary with channels, selective transmission, and selective exposure or deflection.

activation_trace.role: Withholding and lowering by reduction supplies calibrated rather than abolished visual access.
Eyesight supplies the access channel explicitly subjected to partial restraint.
Guarding inviolability supplies the protective function of a maintained boundary.
An opening between things supplies the aperture image underlying the protected private zone.
Concealment supplies material that remains behind the boundary rather than being generally displayed.
Traversable gaps make the piled cloud a controlled interface rather than a sealed wall.
Turning away supplies selective denial of passage or impact.
The endangered eyes tie boundary regulation back to the focus ayah's visual endpoint.
Permission supplies explicit authorization for crossing a privacy boundary.
A concealed private exposure supplies the reason that access is timed and selective.

structural_cues: 24:30 uses min with absar for partial reduction, while 24:43 combines rain through khilal with a final threat to al-absar.
The surah repeatedly distinguishes protected interiors, apertures, appearance, concealment, and authorized access.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies reduced gaze, guarded openings, hidden display, timed permission, and the focus's gap plus hit-or-divert pattern; I infer a shared control-of-access mechanism. A fully live alternative keeps the focus as meteorology with no social-boundary analogy.

changed_reading.before: Rain escapes through accidental holes in a cloud mass.
changed_reading.after: The cloud functions as a governed interface: its boundary is preserved while channels admit selected transmission, and both exposure and impact remain regulated.

context_deltas.mechanism: The slander sequence presents a mutually supporting group, overflowing into a matter, speech received tongue-to-tongue, and indecency spreading. Those operations activate the focus verbs as a process analogue: fragments are driven together, joined, amplified into a dense mass, released through interfaces, and made to land unevenly.

activation_trace.role: A group that surrounds and mutually supports supplies the social aggregate from which circulation begins.
Speech or report spreading like overflow supplies expansion beyond its initial group.
Receiving and taking up speech supplies transfer from one mouth to another.
Diffusion and public spread supplies the report's widening field.
Joining dispersed parts supplies the report's compositional aggregation.
Piling part upon part supplies amplification into an apparently solid mass.
Passage through gaps supplies release through interpersonal interfaces.
Arrival at a target supplies the uneven landing of consequences on persons.

structural_cues: Before the focus, the report sequence advances group -> overflow -> oral reception -> diffusion; the focus advances drive -> join -> pile -> emergence -> targeted impact.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies both process sequences; I supply the arrow that treats cloud dynamics as an analogue for report aggregation and circulation. A live alternative denies any cross-domain mapping and reads the shared process shape as accidental.

changed_reading.before: Cloud pieces combine until precipitation falls.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, the weather process also exposes how small transmitted elements can be socially aggregated into a dense, consequential formation whose outputs land unevenly.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it activates non-dominant mappings of s-m-w to a narrow pore and s-n-w to a flood barrier, neither of which translates sama' or sana here. It remains packet-valid and locally anchored by khilal, descent, and diversion, while 24:35 supplies a niche aperture; downstream prose must label it a form-distant engineering analogy, not lexical meaning.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: Min khilalihi, min al-sama'i, selective descent and diversion, and sana at the endpoint of the hydrologic sequence.

activation_trace.role: The lamp niche as an aperture supplies a context image of controlled passage through an enclosure.
A traversable gap supplies the explicit local channel through the cloud mass.
The split-root image of a narrow pore supplies an exploratory membrane model for the sky source.
Turning flow away supplies active regulation rather than uncontrolled leakage.
A flood barrier that holds and admits water by measure supplies a form-distant metering mechanism at the luminous endpoint.

changed_reading.before: Sky, mountains, gaps, and lightning are locations and effects within a storm.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, the piled sky-mass behaves like a metered membrane: narrow apertures and a barrier regulate stored material, while radiance marks the release threshold.

strongest_changes: The matched near-constructions in 24:35, 24:40, and 24:43, completed by 24:44, recast lightning as the glare edge of calibrated seeing.
The move from mirage-water in 24:39 through causally emerging rain in 24:43 to created life from water in 24:45 turns precipitation into a test of material efficacy.

Gaze, privacy, and permission cues recast the focus cloud's gaps and selective routing as controlled permeability; the slander sequence additionally activates an exploratory aggregation-and-circulation model.
summary.what_was_special: The focus ayah contains both traceable material evidence, rain exiting an assembled body, and spectacle capable of defeating evidence, lightning taking sight. Split mapped branches also expose a tightly contained pore-and-floodgate model that a conservative reading would miss.
remaining_uncertainties: The packet does not settle the syntactic scope of the nested min phrases, the mountains of hail image, or every pronoun referent.
The regulated-aperture and report-circulation readings are structural analogies, not replacements for the meteorological reading.
The membrane and floodgate outlier depends on deliberately form-distant mapped branches and must remain explicitly exploratory.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **The cloud scene is a grammar of aggregation, channeling, and selective outcome.** **Lexical evidence:** fixed-ayah `ز ج و` B001 is gently driving; `ء ل ف` B002 joining separated parts; `ر ك م` B001 heaping; `خ ل ل` B001 an interstice/path through; `و د ق` B003 descending rain; `ص و ب` B001 rain descending, B003 hitting a target, and B004 affliction; `ص ر ف` B001 diversion. **Structural cue:** the repeated `ثم` builds stages from dispersed cloud to heap to output; 24:38 has named rain-like unmeasured provision, and 24:48, at the window's far edge, moves people toward adjudication “between them.” **Assigned role:** gentle motion gathers parts, joining creates a body, interstices channel output, and hitting/diversion distribute differentiated effects. **Abductive move:** the packet gives every stage but not a social analogy; I infer dispersed units → organized whole → channeled, discriminating consequence. **Reading change:** the ayah reads as process logic, showing how subtle direction can culminate in decisive allocation.

2. **A brilliant declaration may arrest sight without yielding substance.** **Lexical evidence:** fixed-ayah `ب ر ق` B001 is visible flash and B004 empty flashing display; `س ن و` B004 is lightning gleam; `ذ ه ب` B006 is taking away; `ب ص ر` B001 is sight. **Structural cue:** the ayah distinguishes rain/hail output from a flash that nearly takes vision; 24:47, within four ayat, distinguishes the brilliant verbal profession “we believed and obeyed” from subsequent turning away. **Assigned role:** flash supplies immediate salience while actual precipitation supplies material consequence. **Abductive move:** the packet supplies spectacle, output, and a nearby speech/action split; I infer that salience can capture perception and conceal lack of yield. This analogy is exploratory. **Reading change:** lightning becomes a warning about confusing impressive signal with productive result, not merely another meteorological detail.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 24:47 retrospectively activated the empty-flash branch by placing impressive profession beside absent yield; 24:48 also sharpened the cloud-process analogy by gathering separated parties toward a discriminating center.

baseline.text: Allah'ın bulutları sürdüğünü, sonra onları birleştirdiğini, sonra da üst üste yığdığını görmedin mi? Ardından yağmurun aralarından çıktığını görürsün. Gökten, oradaki dolu dağlarından dolu indirir; onu dilediğine isabet ettirir, dilediğinden uzaklaştırır. Şimşeğinin parıltısı neredeyse gözleri alır.

findings.text: Bulutların hafifçe sürülmesi, birleşmesi, yığılması ve aralıklardan yağmur çıkarması, verimli sonucun hem parçaların toplanmasına hem geçitlerin korunmasına bağlı olduğunu gösterir.
Aynı inişin birine isabet edip diğerinden çevrilmesi, ortak bir aracın sonucunun yalnız maddesine değil yöneltildiği yere göre ayrıştığını gösterir.
Şimşeğin gerçek ışığı bile görme aracını neredeyse işlemez hale getirebilir; daha fazla aydınlık, algı kapasitesi aşılırsa kendiliğinden daha iyi görüş üretmez.
Şimşeğin göz alıcı parıltısı, etkileyici bir bildirimin görüşü ele geçirip maddi sonuç vermeyebileceği yönünde okunabilir; fakat yakın ayetlerle kurulan bu toplumsal benzetme varsayımsaldır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, görmeyi hem gözle algılama hem de gözün işlevine benzetilen içsel kavrayış olarak kuruyor. Doğrudan göz tanıklığı bu çekirdeğin duyusal gerçekleşimidir; zihinsel görüş, uyku düşü ve başkalarına görünme amacı bu dalın dışında kalır.
